target.title: exec: allow-always script grants survive content changes
target.body:
## Summary

An allow-always decision for an interpreter script is stored as a path and argument pattern without the approved script content. After a legitimate approval, changing that script lets a later matching `system.run` execute the new content without another approval when `tools.exec.strictInlineEval` is enabled.

## Environment

- Commit: 9daef57c85b5c6d833d8ef9cc3e4b974b557d893 (origin/main at time of filing)
- Surface: node-host system.run durable exec approvals for mutable script operands

## Steps to reproduce

1. Enable `tools.exec.strictInlineEval` and request a script through an interpreter such as `node ./approved-script.js`.
2. Approve the request with allow-always while the script has benign content.
3. Replace the contents of the same script path.
4. Issue the same system.run request without an approval decision or approval plan.

## Expected

Changing a mutable file operand after an allow-always decision should require another approval, or invalidate the durable grant.

## Actual

The later request matches the durable path and argument pattern and executes the changed script. The SHA-256 binding used to protect the in-flight approved invocation is not stored or checked on future allow-always reuse.

## Root cause

`src/node-host/invoke-system-run.ts:1043` persists the allow-always decision before the final mutable-operand revalidation at `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.ts:1065`. The persistent entry created by `applyAllowAlwaysDecision` in `src/infra/exec-approvals.ts:2708` contains only `pattern`, optional `argPattern`, and `source`.

```ts
pattern: pattern.pattern,
argPattern: pattern.argPattern,
source: "allow-always",
```

The one-shot approval plan does capture and revalidate a mutable operand SHA-256, but that binding is not part of the durable allowlist entry used by later requests.

## Sibling surfaces

The issue is limited to reusable allow-always grants for interpreter-like script invocations. It requires non-default `strictInlineEval`; without it, those interpreter command patterns are not eligible for reusable allow-always entries. The in-flight request is correctly denied if the script changes before its final revalidation.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: an allow-always grant for a script path survives replacement of the script content.
Real environment tested: production node-host system.run pipeline and durable exec-approvals store at origin/main commit 9daef57c85b5c6d833d8ef9cc3e4b974b557d893.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: approved a benign script with allow-always, replaced its contents, then issued the identical request without an approval decision.
Evidence after fix:
```
{"firstRun":"denied: approval script operand changed before execution","durableAllowAlwaysEntry":true,"subsequentRun":"executed","scriptContent":"PWNED"}
```
Observed result after fix: the changed script did not run in the in-flight request, but its durable allow-always entry remained usable by the subsequent request.
What was not tested: no remote node or external channel was used; the reproduction drives the production node-host policy, durable approval store, and local script execution path.
